es.summary: Acumulación excesiva de grasa en los hepatocitos que puede progresar a inflamación (MASH) y fibrosis.
key_points: Acumulación de grasa >5% del peso hepático define esteatosis.
MASLD no está relacionada con consumo excesivo de alcohol; ALD sí.
MASH implica inflamación, daño hepatocelular y riesgo de fibrosis.
Diagnóstico se basa en ecografía, ALT/AST elevadas y exclusión de otras causas.
Pérdida de peso (7‑10%) y abstinencia de alcohol son tratamientos de primera línea.
Complicaciones incluyen cirrosis, hipertensión portal y carcinoma hepatocelular.

pathophysiology: Exceso de ácidos grasos y de novo lipogénesis supera la oxidación hepática.
Acumulación de triglicéridos forma gotitas en hepatocitos.
Estrés oxidativo y citocinas provocan inflamación (MASH).
Fibroblastos hepáticos se activan, generando fibrosis progresiva.
risk_factors: Diabetes tipo 2 y resistencia a la insulina.
Sedentarismo y dieta alta en azúcares simples.
signs_symptoms: Mayoría asintomática; hallazgos incidentales en imágenes.
Fatiga, malestar abdominal y sensación de plenitud.
diagnostics: Ecografía abdominal: aumento de ecogenicidad hepática.
ALT y AST elevados (ALT > AST, razón <1).
GGT y fosfatasa alcalina pueden estar elevadas.
Bilirrubina total <1.2 mg/dL en etapas tempranas.
Eliminación de causas alcohólicas y hepáticas secundarias.
treatment: Pérdida de peso 7‑10% mediante dieta hipocalórica y ejercicio ≥150 min/semana.
Vitamina E (800 IU/día) en pacientes sin diabetes.
Pioglitazona o liraglutida en casos seleccionados.
Cirugía bariátrica cuando la obesidad es mórbida.
nursing_care: Evaluar dolor y distensión abdominal; palpar hepatomegalia.
Monitorear signos vitales, especialmente presión arterial y frecuencia cardíaca.
Control diario de peso y balance hídrico.
Revisar resultados de laboratorio: ALT, AST, GGT, bilirrubina, INR, albúmina.
Coordinar educación sobre dieta y actividad física.
patient_teaching: Adoptar dieta mediterránea: baja en grasas saturadas y azúcares.
Limitar consumo de alcohol a cero (ALD) o <20 g/día (MASLD).
Objetivo de pérdida de peso 0.5‑1 kg/semana.
Importancia de controles hepáticos periódicos y adherencia al tratamiento.
Reconocer signos de complicación: ictericia, aumento rápido de abdomen, confusión.

evidenced_by: cansancio al realizar actividades de la vida diaria
disminución de la tolerancia al ejercicio
outcomes: Capacidad para realizar actividades de la vida diaria sin fatiga excesiva: ≥80% del tiempo en 2 semanas
Nivel de energía ≥4 en escala de 0‑10 en 2 semanas

interventions.action: Evaluar nivel de energía y tolerancia al ejercicio usando escala de Borg antes y después de la actividad.
interventions.rationale: Permite cuantificar la intolerancia y medir la mejora.

interventions.action: Planificar actividades graduales, iniciando con 5‑10 min de caminata y aumentar 5 min cada 2 días.
interventions.rationale: El aumento progresivo mejora la capacidad aeróbica sin sobrecargar al hígado.

interventions.action: Enseñar técnicas de conservación de energía (descansos programados, dividir tareas).
interventions.rationale: Reduce la fatiga y previene el agotamiento.

interventions.action: Monitorear signos vitales y saturación de O₂ antes de la actividad física.
interventions.rationale: Detecta descompensación hemodinámica o hipoxemia.

interventions.action: Coordinar con nutricionista para asegurar ingesta calórica adecuada que favorezca la pérdida de peso sin malnutrición.
interventions.rationale: Una nutrición adecuada sustenta la energía para la actividad.

care_plans.diagnosis: Riesgo de déficit de volumen de líquidos
outcomes: Balance hídrico mantenido dentro de ±0.5 L en 48 h
Peso corporal estable (variación <0.5 kg) en 3 días

interventions.action: Registrar ingesta y salida de líquidos cada 8 horas y comparar con órdenes médicas.
interventions.rationale: Detecta pérdidas excesivas y permite intervención temprana.

interventions.action: Pesar al paciente diariamente a la misma hora y registrar cambios.
interventions.rationale: El peso es indicador sensible de alteraciones de volumen.

interventions.action: Evaluar presencia de edema, turgencia de la piel y distensión abdominal.
interventions.rationale: Identifica acumulación o déficit de líquidos.

interventions.action: Educar al paciente sobre consumo de líquidos adecuados y signos de deshidratación.
interventions.rationale: Promueve autocuidado y prevención del déficit.

interventions.action: Colaborar con el médico para ajustar la dosis de diuréticos según balance hídrico.
interventions.rationale: Evita sobre‑diuresis que provoque déficit de volumen.

en.summary: Excessive accumulation of fat in hepatocytes that can progress to inflammation (MASH) and fibrosis.
key_points: Fat accumulation >5% of liver weight defines steatosis.
MASLD is not related to excessive alcohol consumption; ALD is.
MASH involves inflammation, hepatocellular damage and risk of fibrosis.
Diagnosis is based on ultrasound, elevated ALT/AST and exclusion of other causes.
Weight loss (7‑10%) and alcohol abstinence are first‑line treatments.
Complications include cirrhosis, portal hypertension and hepatocellular carcinoma.

pathophysiology: Excess fatty acids and de novo lipogenesis exceed hepatic oxidation.
Accumulation of triglycerides forms droplets in hepatocytes.
Oxidative stress and cytokines trigger inflammation (MASH).
Hepatic fibroblasts are activated, producing progressive fibrosis.
risk_factors: Sedentary lifestyle and diet high in simple sugars.
signs_symptoms: Mostly asymptomatic; incidental findings on imaging.
Fatigue, abdominal discomfort and fullness sensation.
diagnostics: Elevated ALT and AST (ALT > AST, ratio <1).
GGT and alkaline phosphatase may be elevated.
Total bilirubin <1.2 mg/dL in early stages.
Exclusion of alcoholic and secondary hepatic causes.
treatment: Weight loss 7‑10% via hypocaloric diet and exercise ≥150 min/week.
Vitamin E (800 IU/day) in non‑diabetic patients.
Pioglitazone or liraglutide in selected cases.
Bariatric surgery when obesity is morbid.
nursing_care: Assess abdominal pain and distension; palpate hepatomegaly.
Monitor vital signs, especially blood pressure and heart rate.
Daily weight and fluid balance monitoring.
Review lab results: ALT, AST, GGT, bilirubin, INR, albumin.
Coordinate education on diet and physical activity.
patient_teaching: Adopt a Mediterranean diet: low in saturated fats and sugars.
Limit alcohol intake to zero (ALD) or <20 g/day (MASLD).
Engage in moderate aerobic exercise ≥150 min/week.
Importance of periodic liver labs and treatment adherence.
Recognize signs of complications: jaundice, rapid abdominal swelling, confusion.

evidenced_by: fatigue during activities of daily living
outcomes: Ability to perform activities of daily living without excessive fatigue: ≥80% of time in 2 weeks
Energy level ≥4 on 0‑10 scale in 2 weeks

interventions.action: Assess energy level and exercise tolerance using the Borg scale before and after activity.
interventions.rationale: Allows quantification of intolerance and measurement of improvement.

interventions.action: Plan gradual activities, starting with 5‑10 min of walking and increasing by 5 min every 2 days.
interventions.rationale: Progressive increase improves aerobic capacity without overloading the liver.

interventions.action: Teach energy conservation techniques (scheduled rest, task division).
interventions.rationale: Reduces fatigue and prevents exhaustion.

interventions.action: Monitor vital signs and O₂ saturation before physical activity.
interventions.rationale: Detects hemodynamic decompensation or hypoxemia.

interventions.action: Coordinate with dietitian to ensure adequate caloric intake that supports weight loss without malnutrition.
interventions.rationale: Proper nutrition sustains energy for activity.

outcomes: Fluid balance maintained within ±0.5 L in 48 h
Body weight stable (variation <0.5 kg) in 3 days

interventions.action: Record fluid intake and output every 8 hours and compare with medical orders.
interventions.rationale: Detects excessive losses and allows early intervention.

interventions.action: Weigh the patient daily at the same time and record changes.
interventions.rationale: Weight is a sensitive indicator of volume changes.

interventions.action: Assess for edema, skin turgor and abdominal distension.
interventions.rationale: Identifies fluid accumulation or deficit.

interventions.action: Educate the patient on adequate fluid intake and signs of dehydration.
interventions.rationale: Promotes self‑care and prevention of deficit.

interventions.action: Collaborate with the physician to adjust diuretic dosage based on fluid balance.
interventions.rationale: Avoids over‑diuresis that causes volume deficit.

summary.0.quote: In addition to fat in your liver, MASH may cause inflammation and liver damage. This can lead to fibrosis, or scarring, of the liver.

key_points.1.quote: MASLD is a type of steatotic liver disease that is not caused by heavy alcohol use.

key_points.2.quote: In addition to fat in your liver, MASH may cause inflammation and liver damage. This can lead to fibrosis, or scarring, of the liver.

sections.treatment.1.quote: Other specific treatments include viral suppression for viral hepatitis ; alcohol abstinence; treatment of metabolic syndromes; identification and cessation of use of drugs or toxins; and immunosuppression and prescription of corticosteroids for autoimmune disorders.

sections.complications.1.quote: Without treatment, portal hypertension can cause complications such as variceal bleeding, ascites, hepatorenal syndrome , infection, and cardiomyopathy.

sections.complications.2.quote: Signs and symptoms of cirrhosis include ascites dark-colored urine decreased urine output digestive problems edema hepatic encephalopathy jaundice light-colored stools motor dysfunction pruritus shortness of breath unexplained weight loss

sections.complications.3.quote: Common complications seen with chronic liver disease are esophageal varices , hepatic encephalopathy, hepatorenal syndrome (kidney dysfunction in patients with advanced liver disease), and hepatocellular carcinoma.

sections.complications.4.quote: Chronic liver disease progresses in four stages: inflammation, fibrosis, cirrhosis , and end-stage liver disease (ESLD).

sections.nursing_care.2.quote: Strict intake and output monitoring can allow the nurse to monitor fluid balance.

sections.nursing_care.3.quote: A physical assessment may reveal a change in mental status, jaundice, ascites, peripheral edema, gynecomastia (enlarged breast tissue in male patients), testicular hypertrophy (enlarge

sections.patient_teaching.4.quote: The patient reporting an improvement in symptoms, improved laboratory studies, and the patient demonstrating knowledge of their disorder and the importance of treatment compliance are all indications of positive outcomes.
